question:
A 4-month-old girl is brought to the physician by her father because he is concerned that she appears sickly and lethargic. She has always had a pale complexion, but it has been getting worse over the past month. She was delivered at home at 36 weeks to a 26-year-old woman following an uncomplicated pregnancy. She has not yet been examined by a physician. She is in the 2nd percentile for head circumference, 10th percentile for length, and 8th percentile for weight. Physical exam shows a pale infant with facial features of micrognathia, flat nasal bridge, and microopthalmos. The eyes are set widely apart and strabismus is present. She has a high arched palate and there is fusion of the cervical vertebrae with flaring of the skin around the neck. A 4/6 holosystolic murmur is heard best on the left chest. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 6.6 g/dL
Hematocrit 20%
Leukocytes 5400/mm3
Platelets 183,000/mm3
Mean corpuscular hemoglobin 41.3 pg/cell
Mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration 33% Hb/cell
Mean corpuscular volume 125 μm3
This patient is most likely to have which of the following findings?"?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Micrognathia, flat nasal bridge, microphthalmos, widely set eyes, strabismus, high arched palate, fusion of cervical vertebrae with skin flaring around the neck" -> "Possible genetic syndrome or chromosomal abnormality" -> "Increased risk for congenital heart defects" -> "Holosystolic murmur heard on physical exam" -> "Likely ventricular septal defect" -> 80%
enhanced_information: The patient's presentation with micrognathia, flat nasal bridge, microphthalmos, widely set eyes, strabismus, high arched palate, fusion of cervical vertebrae, and a holosystolic murmur suggests a possible genetic syndrome or chromosomal abnormality with an increased risk for congenital heart defects, likely a ventricular septal defect. The low hemoglobin and hematocrit levels indicate severe anemia. Therefore, the most likely finding in this patient is mild neutropenia (opa).

The low hemoglobin and hematocrit levels indicate severe anemia. Given the context provided, the most likely finding in this patient is mild neutropenia, which aligns with the enhanced information.
